title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No mathematical error is visible. Implicit points: Aff must be a split extension, i.e. the S_3 × Galois action on the Fermat tower is defined over Q compatibly with a base splitting. Normalizations for even n (x^n + y^n = 1 versus x^n + y^n + z^n = 0, sign issues) are not addressed.

The single geometric point -j does not by itself give a section of M_{0,3} → Γ_Q × S_3. Its decomposition group covers only the index-2 stabilizer of -j, since Galois and S_3 swap -j and -j^2. The full lifting comes from the Galois cover U_∞ → [U/S_3]_Q, with -j used only to rigidify the conjugacy class. The page is consistent with this but does not say it.
The groups G_{p,σ} and μ_G (from (232)) are not defined on this page, so the claimed isomorphism G_{p,σ}^S/μ_G ≅ S^{+^}/μ_S cannot be checked here.

ideas.what: S_3-equivariant arithmetic fundamental group of P^1-{0,1,∞}, based at the order-3 orbifold point -j (j-invariant 0), as an extension of Γ_Q × S_3 by π_1^geom
ideas.modern_name: étale fundamental group of the quotient stack [M_{0,4}/S_3] (j-line orbifold), the S_3 symmetry underlying the hexagon relations of GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, Teichmüller tower); developed by Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,4}, M_{1,1} and Galois action in general terms; this precise S_3/base point -j setup appears only in the Longue Marche continuation notes

ideas.what: Fermat tower as the maximal abelian cover U_∞ of P^1-{0,1,∞}, with automorphism group Aff = \hat M ⋊ (\hat Z^* × S_3); the class of liftings M_{0,3} → Aff encodes the tower via descent
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the pro-Fermat tower / abelianized fundamental group (Ihara's universal Fermat tower)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1986, Annals), Anderson (hyperadelic gamma function, 1989), Coleman
ideas.where_published: not in published texts as far as known

ideas.what: M_1 = M_{0,3}/[π^,π^] is a split extension of Γ_Q × S_3 by \hat M (pullback of the split Aff along χ×id), with splittings parametrized by points of U_∞ over -j
ideas.modern_name: triviality of the Galois action on π_1^ab beyond the cyclotomic character (abelian level of the Ihara program)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore / Ihara, Deligne (tangential base point version)

ideas.what: Comparing the Fermat-tower lifting with a canonical homomorphism (218) M_{0,3} → G_{p,σ}/μ_G whose geometric restriction is the abelianizing quotient of S^{+^}_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: comparison of descent data of the Fermat tower with a model homomorphism (precursor of Jacobi-sum / gamma-function computations of the metabelian Galois action)
ideas.usually_credited_to: closest later work: Ihara, Anderson, Coleman, Deligne

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes identifying the canonical class of liftings M_{0,3} → Aff coming from the Fermat tower with his canonical homomorphisms (217)/(218) into G_{p,σ}/μ_G. Done fully S_3-equivariantly and based at the CM/orbifold point -j rather than at a tangential base point.
missed.quote: Cela conduirait à mettre, si possible, ces relèvements en correspondance avec les homom. (217) ... Reprenons l'hom M_{0,3} → Aff (238), il s'insère dans une suite exacte (240)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Ihara and Anderson treated the abelian and metabelian Galois action on Fermat towers using tangential base points at 0. An S_3-symmetric formulation based at the j=0 orbifold point, compared with a canonical group-theoretic model, is not standard. It might give a symmetric normalization of the Ihara/Anderson invariants.

missed.claim: The page links the pro-Fermat tower (abelian covers of P^1-{0,1,∞}) with the orbifold fundamental group of the j-line (S^{+^}, presumably the completion of PSL_2(Z)), via the quotient that abelianizes π_{0,3}^.
missed.quote: G_{p,σ}^S/μ_G ≃ S^{+^}/μ_S, extension de S_3 ⊂ Z^*×S_3 par M^
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This bridges Fermat-curve arithmetic with the modular (M_{1,1}) side of the Teichmüller tower at the metabelian level. The literature usually keeps these two strands separate.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics proved on the page (splitting of the abelianized extension via the Fermat tower) is standard and essentially routine. The mild interest lies in the S_3-equivariant, CM-point-based formulation and the unrealized plan to match the Fermat descent datum with a canonical model homomorphism. That is an early, unpublished anticipation of Ihara–Anderson-type work, not a hidden finished result.
transcription_corrections: In (239) and (240), 'M^' denotes \hat M (abelianized profinite π_{0,3}).
'Abstrait' is more plausibly 'obtenu' ('obtenu "en rendant π_{0,3}^ abélien"').

In (240), the right-hand term of the top row is written as N_{0,3} (heavily corrected), with a marginal annotation '≃ Γ_Q × S_3'. It is not simply written Γ_Q × S_3. The next page indeed uses N_{0,3}.
The base point is written '-j' (minus j), as in π_1(U_{0,3,Q}, S_3; -j). It is not \bar\jmath.
The crossed-out symbol before 'M_1' in the last lines appears to be a struck subscripted symbol (perhaps M_{0,3} or N_{0,3}), replaced by M_1.
In the second display, the transcription has 'μ_G' after G_{p,σ}; the image subscript looks like 'μ_G' or 'μ_a', and 'μ_S' after S^{+^}.
